request.spec:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in

agent.result_text:
Bulk settle is now all-or-nothing, and all 4 e2e tests pass with `bin/e2e`: the main "batch all or nothing" test and scenarios 1–3.

The change is in the server, in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/BulkSettleClaims.java`, which now works in two passes:

1. **Check every selected claim** using the same rules as settling one claim. If any one would be refused, nothing is saved, logged or audited, and the response is `settled 0, refused <number selected>`. Going to PENDING doesn't count as a refusal. A selected claim that isn't on the sheet, an archived sheet, or a viewer also makes the whole batch refused.
2. **Otherwise, settle them all in list order** as before, with the same per-claim lines. Then one extra audit line is written: `BATCH_SETTLED sheet=<id> by=<user> batch=<n> count=<claims in batch> total=<sum of frozen dues>`. The count includes claims that went to PENDING. The total only adds up claims that ended SETTLED, and a settled claim with no due figure (`n/a`) adds nothing.

I also updated the comment at the top of `bulk-settle.POST.yml` to describe the new behaviour. The front end didn't need changing because it only shows the settled and refused counts the server returns.

probe.probe_text:
I've read the whole application (about 250 Java step classes, the repositories, the SQL and Java migrations, and the React features) and changed nothing. Names below are the code's own; `file:line` points to where each rule lives. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## The core numbers (server: `claim/Dues.java`, `rollup/Rollup.java`; client: `features/rates/api.ts`) **The sheet's today** (`SheetRepository.today`) is the date nearly every rule uses. A new sheet starts on the real date and a user can set it (`today.POST`). **"In force on a date"** means the value with the latest from-date on or before that date; a value with no from-date applies from the beginning of time. This same rule is written separately for grades (`Person.gradeOn`), rates (`Rollup.rateOn`, `RateRepository.find/inForce`) and dated settings (`DatedSetting.on`), and again in the front end (`gradeOn`, `rateOn`, `settingOn`). A rate past its to-date is n/a. **A claim's rate figure** (`Dues.of`) is amount × the rate of the person's grade on the claim's date ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimals. - **Rounding** (`Dues.Late.rounding`): half up when the claim's `roundDate` is before the `policy-date`, half to even on or after it. A blank policy date means the sheet's today, so the boundary moves with the date. - A correction's `roundDate` is the date of the claim it corrects. **A claim's shown due** (`Dues.shown`, `Claim.due`), in order of precedence: 1. `settledDue`, if it was frozen at settlement. 2. Otherwise the figure a statement bound it to (`statedDue`), but only if the claim is not PENDING. 3. Otherwise the live rate figure. On top of 2 or 3: - **Late charge** (`Dues.charge`) is added. It compounds once for each full 30 days past `lateFrom`, which is due-by plus the grace days of the person's grade (`grace-`). Each 30-day step uses the `late-pct` in force on that boundary date and is rounded by the policy date. - No late charge applies to a correction, a claim that isn't OPEN/PENDING, a deferred claim, or a claim with no figure. - **Floor** comes last: at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). A correction gets no floor. - With no rate the due is **n/a**. **Which claims count** (`Claim.isCounting`, `Person.countsLive` / `leftOutLive`; client `counts`, `liveClaims`): - Only OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count. - Of those, a live total leaves out: - a deferred claim; - an open claim with no statement binding it that is dated inside one of the person's holds; - every open unbound claim once the person's retirement date is reached (`isRetiredReached`). **Per-person figures** (`Rollup.Figures`; client `People.tsx`): - `person-claimed`: the sum of amounts of the counting live claims. - `person-due-total` (`personDue`): the sum of shown dues, n/a ones skipped, capped at the `cap` in force on today. - It is **n/a** when the person's grade has no rate today and no claim "keeps" a figure. - A claim keeps a figure if it is settled, bound, or has a rate and was either dated on or before today or graded differently from today. - `person-excess`: the amount above the cap. - `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` (`splitDues`): uncapped. - `person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`. - `person-aged-0-30`, `person-aged-31-60`, `person-aged-61`: the dues of open claims, bucketed by days since the claim's date. - `person-period-

-due-total` (`personPeriodDue`). - `person-active`: has an open live claim dated within the last 30 days. - `person-backing`: the frozen settled dues of their patrons' claims dated within the last 90 days. **Sheet totals:** - `rollup-claimed-total`: a plain sum. - `rollup-due-total` and `rollup-overdue-total`: `trimmedSum`, which drops the single highest and single lowest person when there are 3 or more. - `rollup-settled-total` and `rollup-open-total`: plain sums. - `rollup-overdue-count`. - `tag--due-total`, `month--due-total` (by the claim's date). - Summary (`Summary.tsx`): per grade, the count, due and active count of people not retired; the due per period; claims per status; claims per void reason. **Per-claim fields:** - `claim-due`. - `claim-due-by`: the `terms`-th business day after the date, skipping weekends and holidays (`BusinessDays.dueBy`). Terms come from the person's own terms, else `terms-`, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14). - `claim-overdue`: open, not deferred, and `lateFrom` is before today. - `claim-period`: the period that contains the **due-by**, not the claim's date. - `claim-number`: given at open. It is sheet-wide, or `-` / `X-` once `period-numbering-from` is on or before today. It is kept on void. - `claim-stated`, `claim-deferred` (OPEN and `deferredUntil` after today, computed in SQL in `ClaimRepository.COLUMNS`), `claim-late-entry`, `claim-batch`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-reminded`, the log lines and the comment lines. ## What is frozen, and when - **Settle** (`SettleClaim`): freezes the shown due, including today's late charge. With no rate nothing is frozen and the due stays live. - **Approve**: freezes the PENDING claim's live figure. - **Re-settle**: re-freezes the due as if the claim were open and unbound. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): - records the capped due-total (or n/a) and binds each counting claim to its rate figure. The late charge and floor are not bound and keep moving. - unbinds everything else. - can be taken "as of" a past date using the history tables. - **Cancel statement**: unbinds every claim and does not restore the earlier bindings. - **Period close / soft-close** (`PeriodClosing.fixNow`): - freezes the period total and each person's total from claims whose due-by is in the period. - status is taken from the claim log at the period's last day, but holds and deferral are judged as they are now. - **Void of a SETTLED claim**: takes its frozen figure out of every total. - **Due-by** is fixed when a claim is added. Edit and re-date do not move it, but adding a holiday re-works it for claims that aren't SETTLED/VOID (`refixDueBys`). ## Who may do what - **Roles** (`RoleRepository.roleOf`): clerk is the default; steward and viewer are assigned. A delegation that covers today makes the user steward. Only a steward by their own assigned role can delegate. - **Viewers and archived sheets**: `RefuseViewer` blocks every change when the sheet is archived or the user is a viewer. The bulk endpoints check this inside the code instead of in the YAML pipeline. - **Permission matrix** (`Permissions.java`), `perm-`: - open, settle, void and close: clerk or steward. - reassign and reopen: steward. - **Steward only**: approve, reject (needs a reason), re-date, re-settle, cancel statement, void a SETTLED claim (within 7 days of its SETTLED log date), archive. - **Four eyes**: the user who opened or last edited a claim cannot settle or approve it. - **Clerk limit**: a clerk settling a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit` sends it to PENDING instead. - **Proof threshold** (`proof-threshold-`, else the sheet's): blocks settle or approve when the claim has no proofs. - **Note threshold**: blocks opening a claim with an empty note. - **Settings, rates, roles, holidays and void reasons can be changed by any non-viewer.** That includes a clerk assigning themselves steward. ## Status, dates and refusals - **Status flow** (`ClaimStatus.moveTo`): DRAFT → OPEN; OPEN → SETTLED or PENDING; PENDING → SETTLED or back to OPEN. DRAFT, OPEN and PENDING can go to VOID. - Only a DRAFT can be edited, and editing takes a lock. - Only an OPEN claim can be deferred or split. - OPEN and PENDING claims can be reminded, once per today. - **Closed period** (`requireOpen`): refuses almost every claim action when the claim's **due-by** falls in a closed period. - A soft-closed period refuses nothing; a claim added into it is marked as a late entry. - With `grace-days` set, changing today auto-closes periods that are past their grace days, skipping soft-closed ones. - **Retirement**: a claim dated after the retirement date is refused on add, edit, re-date and reassign. - **Correction**: a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person. - **Reference**: unique on the sheet, ignoring case. - **Void reason**: required once the sheet has any. - **Bulk actions**: - Bulk settle is all-or-nothing, and records a batch number and a `BATCH_SETTLED` audit line. - Bulk open and bulk reassign go claim by claim. - Bulk grade gives a viewer a count of 0 rather than an error. - **Paste import**: each line is checked like a single add and the whole paste is all-or-nothing. A note ending in ` #ref` sets the reference. Tags are not carried. - **Quick add**: creates the person with grade A if they are new. - **Default dates**: a blank date takes `entry-date`, else today. **Except edit, which uses today.** - **Changing today** writes a `SNAPSHOT` audit line per person, keeps an as-of copy of the sheet, and releases all claim locks. `?shown-asof=` gives a read-only view of the sheet as of a date. ## Inconsistencies I noticed - `Summary` leaves out anyone with a retirement date at all, even a future one. The rollup still counts them. - `ClosePeriod`'s doc comment says claims "whose date falls in it", but the code uses the due-by. - `ClaimedTotal`'s doc says OPEN and SETTLED, but the code also counts PENDING. - Adding a holiday can move a claim's due-by into a closed period without any check. - Re-dating or editing a claim changes its rate, grade, floor, hold and rounding dates but not its due-by or period. # 2. How hard it was to follow It was hard, because the logic is scattered and partly duplicated. Server rules are split across about 250 single-method step classes, YAML pipelines and SQL fragments (for example, "deferred" is computed in a SQL string). More importantly, every on-screen figure is computed a second time in TypeScript (`rates/api.ts`, `claims/api.ts`, `periods/api.ts`, `settings/api.ts`), separately from the server's `Dues`/`Rollup` that feeds the audit file, and the "in force on a date" rule alone exists about six times. A new developer would need to read both sides and keep them in lockstep: there's no single place that owns "how a due is worked out".
